head: 7c8b749f4ca2f69c01de5e3d86d419b713d85344
executive_summary: The repository is a hardened, previously-audited codebase whose server half is in good shape: 37 of 37 Node tests pass against a real PostgreSQL 18.4 with zero skips and 78.34% measured line coverage, npm audit reports zero vulnerabilities at every severity, no secret is present in tracked files, and the full money path — completion gate, dispute freeze, idempotent refund, balanced ledger — is executed green. R_point is 79.07 (grade B) with a 95% band of [72.76, 84.83]. The blockers are not code quality; they are unverified promises: no CI job runs the server suite, every Android CI run in history has failed, the declared escrow cron can never start, no backup has ever been restored, and the Android client never calls 13 of the 18 authenticated routes. Six P1 findings cap P_GO at 0.35 and the verdict is NO-GO — REMEDIABLE. Seven tasks below remove four P1s and four P2s; the three remaining P1s (client wiring, Android CI, backup drill) and the legal sign-off need work this session cannot execute.

tasks.title: Stop counting failed OTP sends against the per-window send budget
tasks.change_spec: In POST /v1/auth/request-otp, the window query at server.js:277-283 selects every otp_challenges row created inside OTP_SEND_WINDOW_MINUTES with no status filter, so a row is counted even when the Kavenegar call at server.js:316-325 failed and wrote status='failed'. Add `AND status <> 'failed'` to that query so a provider outage cannot consume the budget of a user who never received a code. Do NOT change OTP_MAX_SENDS_PER_WINDOW, the 60-second resend cooldown, the advisory lock, the expiry, or the row write on failure — the failed row must still be recorded for diagnostics. Do not touch the verify-otp route.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN three otp_challenges rows for one phone with status='failed' created seconds ago WHEN POST /v1/auth/request-otp is called for that phone THEN the response is NOT 429
GIVEN three otp_challenges rows with status='pending' created seconds ago WHEN POST /v1/auth/request-otp is called THEN the response is 429 with error 'too_many_requests'
Command `cd services/auth-api && AUDIT_DATABASE_URL=... npm test` exits 0 with 0 skipped
Existing behaviour outside scope remains unchanged: 37 pre-existing tests still pass
tasks.rollback: git revert <commit> — the change is one SQL predicate and two new test cases, with no schema or data migration.

tasks.title: Add an OTP-challenge retention job so expired login rows stop accumulating
tasks.change_spec: Add src/retention.js exporting purgeExpiredOtpChallenges(client,{olderThanDays}) which deletes otp_challenges rows whose created_at is older than the window and whose status is not 'pending', plus a CLI entry point (`node src/retention.js run`) that reads OTP_RETENTION_DAYS (default 7) and reports the number of rows removed. Scope note recorded during execution: escrow_holds rows are deliberately NOT purged because they are accounting records; the original finding text implied both tables and is narrowed here. Add the npm script `retention`. Document the window in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md and the variable in services/auth-api/.env.example. Do not delete rows with status='pending' or 'sending' — a live login may still be in flight — and do not touch the account-erasure path.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an otp_challenges row with created_at 30 days ago and status='verified' WHEN the purge runs THEN the row is gone and the return value counts it
GIVEN an otp_challenges row with created_at 30 days ago and status='pending' WHEN the purge runs THEN the row is still present
Command `node src/retention.js run` against the disposable database exits 0 and prints a count
Command `npm test` in services/auth-api exits 0 with 0 skipped
tasks.rollback: Delete src/retention.js, its test and the npm script. No schema change, so no data rollback is required.

tasks.title: Provide an executable local gate that reproduces the proposed server CI job
tasks.change_spec: Add scripts/ci-server-check.sh: requires AUDIT_DATABASE_URL and a working node; runs `npm ci`, `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`, `node --check` over src/*.js, asserts every db/NNN_*.sql has a matching db/down/NNN_*.down.sql, performs a full migration round trip (up -> down 99 with CONFIRM_DESTRUCTIVE_ROLLBACK=yes -> up), runs `node --test --experimental-test-coverage`, and fails the build if the summary contains `# skipped` with a non-zero count. This is the executable half of F-EXEC-004 that does not depend on the workflows permission. It must not weaken, skip or delete any existing test. Document it in docs/TESTING.md.
acceptance_criteria: Command `AUDIT_DATABASE_URL=... bash scripts/ci-server-check.sh` exits 0
The script fails (exit non-zero) when AUDIT_DATABASE_URL is unset
The script fails when the runner reports skipped tests
Existing behaviour outside scope remains unchanged
tasks.rollback: Delete scripts/ci-server-check.sh and the docs/TESTING.md paragraph.

tasks.title: Install the server CI workflow into .github/workflows
tasks.change_spec: Copy ci/proposed/server.yml to .github/workflows/server.yml unchanged and commit. This is the repository's own documented highest-yield action. If GitHub rejects the push because the installation token lacks the `workflows` permission, that is an external permission boundary: record the exact error, do not retry with a workaround, and leave ci/proposed/server.yml as the shippable artifact for a maintainer.
acceptance_criteria: Either .github/workflows/server.yml exists on the branch and a run appears in `gh run list`, OR the push fails with the documented workflows-permission error and the exact stderr is recorded
ci/proposed/README.md is updated with the observed outcome
tasks.verification_command: git ls-tree --name-only HEAD .github/workflows/ && gh run list --limit 3
tasks.rollback: git revert <commit>; if the file was rejected at push time nothing was ever created.
tasks.human_reason: Only if the push is rejected: a maintainer with the GitHub `workflows` permission must run the one-line cp+commit shown in ci/proposed/README.md.

tasks.title: Make the declared escrow cron actually run the escrow worker
tasks.change_spec: The cron service oosta-escrow-release currently inherits the auth-api image CMD `sh -c "npm run migrate && npm start"`, which boots a web server instead of the worker, and its environment pins FEATURE_ESCROW_RELEASE="false", which makes the target route answer 503. Give the cron a `dockerCommand` that runs `node src/escrow-worker.js`, and give the cron only the variables the worker reads (PLATFORM_API_BASE_URL, ESCROW_WORKER_TOKEN, NODE_ENV). Remove FEATURE_ESCROW_RELEASE from the cron block and change it on the web service to an operator-set `sync: false` value with a comment that escrow release stays fail-closed until approved. FEATURE_ESCROW_RELEASE must NOT default to true anywhere. Add a test that parses the YAML and asserts the cron's command invokes escrow-worker.js and that no cron variable sets FEATURE_ESCROW_RELEASE true.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN render.yaml WHEN parsed as YAML THEN the cron job's command contains src/escrow-worker.js
GIVEN render.yaml WHEN parsed as YAML THEN neither service sets FEATURE_ESCROW_RELEASE to "true"
Command `cd services/auth-api && node --test test/render-blueprint.test.js` exits 0
Command `npm test` in services/auth-api exits 0 with 0 skipped
tasks.verification_command: cd services/auth-api && node --test test/render-blueprint.test.js; echo EXIT=$?
tasks.rollback: git revert <commit>; render.yaml only takes effect on the next Blueprint sync, so a revert before the next sync changes nothing in the running environment.
tasks.requires_human: The escape hatch in Render's cron schema (`dockerCommand`) is applied as declared configuration; enabling FEATURE_ESCROW_RELEASE remains an operator decision and is deliberately left fail-closed.

tasks.title: Exclude the Room database and preferences from pre-API-31 cloud backup
tasks.change_spec: backup_rules.xml feeds fullBackupContent, which Android uses on API 24-30; minSdk is 24. Its <full-backup-content> element is empty, so the Room database (users, devices, orders and the phone number in UserEntity) is uploaded to the user's Google Drive on those devices. Add <exclude domain="database" path="."/> and <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="."/> inside <full-backup-content>, matching what data_extraction_rules.xml already does for API 31+. Do not change android:allowBackup and do not touch data_extraction_rules.xml.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN backup_rules.xml WHEN parsed as XML THEN full-backup-content contains an exclude for the database domain and one for the sharedpref domain
The file still parses as well-formed XML
Existing behaviour outside scope remains unchanged

tasks.title: Record the client-side journey gap as a single tracked specification instead of leaving it implicit
tasks.change_spec: Add a table to docs/GO_60_ROADMAP.md listing, for each of the 18 authenticated server routes, whether app/src/main contains a call site, with the file:line of each existing call site. Add a note to docs/API.md that POST /v1/devices assigns the id and that clients must not mint one. This does not close F-EXEC-001 — no client is written — it converts an implicit gap into an auditable one with a machine-checkable census. Do not claim any capability is implemented.

tasks.title: Execute a real backup and restore drill and record the measured RPO/RTO
tasks.change_spec: On a host with postgresql-client: populate a staging database, run scripts/backup-database.sh, restore the produced .dump with scripts/restore-database.sh into an isolated instance, verify row counts for ledger_entries, ledger_postings and escrow_holds, and record the elapsed time and the newest recoverable transaction in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md. Do NOT substitute a COPY-based dump — the production mechanism is pg_dump --format=custom and testing a different mechanism proves nothing.
acceptance_criteria: A dump file exists and `pg_restore --list` reads it
The restored database has identical row counts for ledger_entries, ledger_postings, escrow_holds, users
docs/DEPLOYMENT.md records RPO and RTO as measured numbers with the date and the host
tasks.verification_command: psql "$RESTORED_URL" -c 'SELECT count(*) FROM ledger_postings' && diff <(psql "$SOURCE_URL" -Atc 'SELECT count(*) FROM ledger_postings') <(psql "$RESTORED_URL" -Atc 'SELECT count(*) FROM ledger_postings')
tasks.rollback: Drop the isolated restore instance; nothing in the source database is mutated.
tasks.human_reason: pg_dump and pg_restore cannot be installed in this sandbox: no apt mirror is reachable and the only npm PostgreSQL distribution ships initdb/pg_ctl/postgres. A human with a postgresql-client host must run it.

Drop `permissions: contents: write` and the force-push in android-apk.yml. Then correct the README sentence that says the Android tests are executed in CI.

tasks.title: Wire the Android client to the server for devices, quotes, payments and the order lifecycle
tasks.change_spec: Add authenticated clients for POST /v1/devices, GET /v1/devices, POST /v1/quotes/:id/accept, POST /v1/technicians/apply, POST /v1/technicians/kyc, POST /v1/orders/:id/quotes|evidence|start|complete|dispute and POST /v1/payments/zarinpal/start, each with a header for Authorization and, where the server requires it, Idempotency-Key. Store the server-returned device UUID as the Room primary key; never synthesise one. Add MockWebServer contract tests asserting path, method, auth header and the exact JSON field names the server returns. Do not weaken the memory-only token store without also adding an encrypted persistence path and its test.

launch_runbook: 1) A maintainer installs .github/workflows/server.yml and fixes build.yml so one Android run is green. 2) Run the backup/restore drill and record RPO/RTO. 3) Counsel signs the four persian texts. 4) Turn on a single flag at a time in the order login -> triage -> bookings -> matching -> payments -> escrow release, watching GET /metrics after each. 5) Before enabling FEATURE_ESCROW_RELEASE, apply T-005 and confirm one hold releases end-to-end. 6) Rollback lever for every step is the corresponding FEATURE_* variable set back to false; for the schema, CONFIRM_DESTRUCTIVE_ROLLBACK=yes plus `node src/migrate.js down N` — every down script drops tables, so take a restore point first. 7) On-call triggers: any 5xx burst on /v1/auth/*, oosta_provider_failures_total increasing for more than 5 minutes, or oosta_escrow_holds_due growing for two consecutive days.
